note_on_method: Each venue page rests on one line of the City of St. George's Pickleball page - a name, a street address and a court count under the heading "City of St. George Pickleball Courts" - plus, for Little Valley, the 2025 programme schedule, the check-in rule and the 2020 article on the same page, and, for Vernon Worthen, one sentence of that article about where the programme began. The US Census address geocoder supplies the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Thirty-three pickleball courts at the City's Little Valley complex, tied for the largest single-venue count on this site and the first venue here published as a dedicated pickleball facility.

The City's line is "Little Valley / 2149 Horseman Park Drive / Courts:  33", and the page heads the venue "Little Valley Pickleball Complex". This is a programmed facility rather than a park with courts in it. The same page carries the City's 2025 schedule, which numbers the courts, reserves "9-32 (24 courts)" for league sessions, six courts for youth sessions, two for adult clinics, and "All 33 Courts" for two tournaments a year.

The City's 2020 article on the same page says the complex was then "home to 24 well-maintained courts" and that it was chosen as "Public Facility of the Year" by the Professional Pickleball Registry. Twenty-four is not thirty-three, and this page does not pretend otherwise. The article is dated 19 August 2020 and describes itself as history; the list is the City's undated present-tense inventory. So thirty-three publishes, and twenty-four is what the venue was.
slots.getting_there:
2149 Horseman Park Drive, St. George, UT 84790. The US Census address geocoder matched the address at house-number level and placed it in Washington County, in the incorporated place St. George city. The Census file spells the street "HORESMAN PARK DR" - a transposition, same number, same type, and the only Horseman Park Drive in the city - and the City's spelling is the one published here.

The City publishes nothing about parking at the complex, and nothing about restrooms. What it does say about arriving is a rule: "Players, please check in with the attendant or instructor to determine if courts are available during the St. George Pickleball programs". Find the attendant before you find a court.
slots.what_to_expect:
A facility with an attendant, a timetable and a numbered court plan, which is a different experience from turning up at a park. During the City's programmes, courts 9 to 32 are reserved for league play on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday mornings and evenings through the Winter and Spring seasons, youth sessions take courts 21-22 and 26-29 on Monday and Wednesday afternoons, and the Rock N Roll Tournament in February and the Southern Shootout in April take all thirty-three courts from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. Outside those times the City states the price: "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them - free of charge".

The City also asks players to "check in with the attendant or instructor", warns that "Times may change based on participation numbers", and takes court reservations through the Parks Department at 435-627-4530. Non-City events need a reservation and possibly a special event permit, displayed on the court.

Nothing is stated about lighting, surface, opening hours or whether any court is covered. The schedule runs evening sessions to 9:30 p.m. in January, but that is a timetable and not a lighting statement, so lighting is recorded as not verified.

faqs.a: Thirty-three, on the City's current list: "Little Valley / 2149 Horseman Park Drive / Courts:  33". The City's 2020 article said twenty-four; that figure is dated and printed here as history.

When the courts are vacant, yes, in the City's own words: "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them - free of charge". During City programmes, courts are reserved and an attendant says what is available.
Not stated. The City schedules league play until 9:30 p.m. on winter evenings but never uses the word lights, and this site records lighting only when the operator states it.

Yes. The City's page carries a "Reserve a Pickleball Court" link and says to contact Parks at 435-627-4530. Non-City events need a reservation and possibly a special event permit, displayed on the court.

faqs.q: Why does the Census spell the street differently?
faqs.a: The Census address file has "HORESMAN PARK DR", a transposition of the City's "Horseman Park Drive". Same number, same street; the City's spelling is published.

slots.description:
Six pickleball courts at Vernon Worthen Park, the place where the City of St. George's pickleball programme began.

The City's line is "Vernon Worthen / 300 S. 400 E. / Courts: 6". Six is the smallest count of the three published venues, and six courts is six games at once. The City's 2020 article on the same page supplies the history: "In 2012, Wayne Bullock established the first pickleball program for the City of St. George on four permanent and two temporary courts at Vernon Worthen Park." It goes on to say that Bullock "creatively launched the ladder league format" here, and that "The league format and scorecard became so popular that the USA Pickleball Association contacted Bullock for permission to adopt it."

So the park has two counts in the City's record: four permanent and two temporary in 2012, and six on the undated current list. They are different kinds of statement, an origin and an inventory, and this page prints both rather than choosing. The count also changed on this site: the imported row said seven courts, and the City's six replaced it.
slots.getting_there:
300 S. 400 E., St. George, UT 84770. That is a Utah grid address - 300 South, 400 East - and the US Census address geocoder resolved it as written, "300 S 400 E, ST GEORGE, UT, 84770", at house-number level, in Washington County and in the incorporated place St. George city, near the centre of St. George. The imported record carried "200 South 400 East", a block away, under the name "Worthen Park"; the City's own line and the City's own name replaced both.

The City publishes nothing about parking or restrooms at this park, and no hours. It is the one published venue in the 84770 postcode; Little Valley and Bloomington are both in 84790.
slots.what_to_expect:
Six courts and no published programme. Everything the City schedules on its pickleball page - leagues, youth sessions, clinics, tournaments - is on a timetable headed Little Valley, and that timetable names no other venue, so nothing on it reserves a court here. What that does not mean is that the courts are free: the City's "free of charge" sentence is about Little Valley, and this page records the price at Vernon Worthen as not stated.

The City also states no hours, no lighting, no surface, and nothing about whether the six courts are dedicated or share ground with tennis, so each of those is unknown rather than assumed from Little Valley. Six courts is six doubles games, twenty-four players on court before anyone waits, which is a workable drop-in number without being a complex.

The one thing the City does say about this park is where it stands in the story. This is where its programme started in 2012, on four permanent and two temporary courts, and where the ladder-league format was launched. The current six is what you will find; the four-plus-two is what was here.

faqs.a: Six, on the City's current list: "Vernon Worthen / 300 S. 400 E. / Courts: 6". The imported record said seven; the City's figure replaced it and the change is logged.
Not stated. The City's "free of charge" sentence is about Little Valley. Nothing is published about the price here, so it is recorded as unknown rather than free.
Not stated. The City says nothing about lighting at any of its pickleball venues, and this site publishes a lighting answer only when the operator states one.
It is where the City's programme began: "In 2012, Wayne Bullock established the first pickleball program for the City of St. George on four permanent and two temporary courts at Vernon Worthen Park."
300 S. 400 E. is a Utah grid address: 300 South, 400 East. The Census geocoder resolves it as written, in postcode 84770, near the centre of the city.

slots.description:
Seven pickleball courts at Bloomington Park in the south-west of St. George, the second-largest count of the three published venues in the city.

The City's whole record of this venue is one line: "Bloomington Park / 650 Man O War Road / Courts: 7". It sits third in the four-line list headed "City of St. George Pickleball Courts", between Vernon Worthen's six and the four at Ledges that cannot be published for want of an address. Seven is an odd number for a block of courts, and the City does not say how they are laid out, whether they were built as pickleball courts, or whether any share a slab with tennis.

Nothing else on the City's page names this park. The 2020 article is about Little Valley and Vernon Worthen; the programme schedule is for Little Valley; the check-in rule and the free-of-charge sentence belong to Little Valley too. So Bloomington is the venue in St. George about which the City states the least, and this page is correspondingly short on everything except the count and the address.
slots.getting_there:
650 Man O War Road, St. George, UT 84790. The US Census address geocoder matched "650 MAN O WAR RD, ST GEORGE, UT, 84790" at house-number level and placed it in Washington County, in the incorporated place St. George city. It shares the 84790 postcode with Little Valley; Vernon Worthen is in 84770. The imported dataset held a row for this park with the city written "Saint George", which is not how the City writes it, so this entry was created from the City's own line rather than matched to that row.

The City publishes nothing about parking, restrooms or hours at this park.
slots.what_to_expect:
Seven courts, and no other stated fact about them. That is the honest summary, and it is worth spelling out what it excludes. The City publishes no price for Bloomington Park - the "free of charge" sentence on its page is about Little Valley - so the fee is recorded as unknown, not as free. It publishes no hours and no lighting, so there is no stated evening window. It publishes no surface. It never calls the courts indoor or outdoor. And it schedules nothing here: every league, clinic and tournament on the City's 2025 programme is timetabled at Little Valley, so nothing on that schedule reserves a court at this park.

For a player, seven courts is seven doubles games at once, twenty-eight people on court before a queue forms, which makes it a more practical drop-in count than Vernon Worthen's six and a very different proposition from Little Valley's thirty-three with an attendant. Whether you will find it busy is not something the City says. If you want a City-run session, a clinic or a reservation, the page points to Little Valley and to the Parks Department at 435-627-4530.
